correctness.rationale: Directly differentiated the printed nonlinear two-species delayed field at (2/3,1/3): B=[[k-2/3,-2/3],[2/3,-1/3]]. Multiplying det(s^q I−e^(−sτ)B)=0 by e^(2sτ) gives z²+(1−k)z+(2−k)/3=0 for z=s^q e^(sτ); its discriminant is (3k−5)(k+1)/3<0. Upper-root argument θ=π−atan(sqrt((5−3k)(k+1)/3)/(1−k)); modulus fixes ω=((2−k)/3)^(10/19). Since θ∈(qπ/2,π), first positive phase is (θ−qπ/2)/ω, earlier than the conjugate branch (2π−θ−qπ/2)/ω; later solutions add 2π/ω. Independent Python complex determinant gave ω=0.908501523595597, τ=1.1477399921500826 and residual 2.25e−16, with positive transversality speed 0.3940683275792385. These are spectral, not a nonlinear Hopf theorem.
residual_risks: Complex powers use the principal branch; nonlinear cycle existence, direction and numerical integrator accuracy are outside the proof.
